chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said narrated from Fadala, from Musa, from Ali ibn Sa'id, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about a man who was caught while digging (for treasure). He said: I do not see cutting (the hand) upon him, unless he is caught and has dug multiple times, then I cut him.

key_terms.قَطْعًا: cutting (referring to the hadd punishment of amputation)

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for cutting the hand of a treasure hunter in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), the condition for applying the hadd of cutting the hand to a treasure hunter (nabbash) is clarified as requiring repeated digging, distinguishing habitual extraction from a single instance. This reflects the Shia juristic principle of avoiding the hadd punishment unless the act demonstrates a persistent pattern of taking what is not explicitly owned, aligning with the broader legal discourse on khums and buried wealth in al-Istibsar.
